statement: a) Determine the minimum value of $\left(x + \dfrac{1}{y}\right)\!\left(x + \dfrac{1}{y} - 2018\right) + \left(y + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)\!\left(y + \dfrac{1}{x} - 2018\right)$ for positive reals $x, y$.\n\nb) Determine the minimum value of $\left(x + \dfrac{1}{y}\right)\!\left(x + \dfrac{1}{y} + 2018\right) + \left(y + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)\!\left(y + \dfrac{1}{x} + 2018\right)$ for positive reals $x, y$.

In Heptanomisma, four coins and three banknotes have seven distinct positive integer denominations; the smallest banknote exceeds the sum of all four coins. A tourist has one of each denomination.

a) Prove that the tourist can purchase a book if each banknote's denomination is less than $49$.

b) Show that the tourist may be unable to purchase the book if the largest banknote has denomination $49$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with orthocenter $H$. Let $D$, $E$, $F$ be the midpoints of $AB$, $AC$, $AH$ respectively. The reflections of $B$ and $C$ across $F$ are $P$ and $Q$.

a) Show that lines $PE$ and $QD$ intersect on the circumcircle of $	riangle ABC$.

b) Prove that lines $PD$ and $QE$ intersect on segment $AH$.

An integer $n \geq 2$ with divisors $1 = d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_s = n$ is 	extit{good} if there exists $k$ with $2 \leq k \leq s$ such that $d_k > 1 + d_1 + \cdots + d_{k-1}$; otherwise it is 	extit{bad}.

a) Show there are infinitely many bad integers.

b) Prove that among any seven consecutive integers greater than $2$, at least four are good.

c) Show there are infinitely many sequences of seven consecutive good integers.
